system_prompt:
You are a fourth-grade student taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in your grade. Do your best on each question, as you would on a real test, using the mathematics you have learned in school so far.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
Draw the line of symmetry on this shape.

[Image: an elongated kite shape figure with two pointy-ends at either end.]

Figure, described in words:
A quadrilateral kite shape oriented diagonally on a blank background. It has a sharp, acute vertex pointing toward the bottom left. From this vertex, two long straight sides of equal length extend upward and to the right: one side goes steeply up and right to an upper vertex, and the other side goes gently up and right to a lower-right vertex. The top side is a short horizontal segment extending rightward from the upper vertex, and the right side is a short vertical segment extending upward from the lower-right vertex, meeting at a top-right corner.

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer: I would draw a line straight down the middle of the kite shape, from the pointy end at the bottom left to the middle of the short horizontal side at the top. The line would go through the middle of the shape, making both sides look like mirror images of each other.
